newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council calls for protection of Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council calls for protection of Palestinians.

text.p: The United States cast the lone abstention late on Saturday when the 14 other members of the Security Council called for the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be ensured and for the immediate resumption of the Middle East peace process.

The resolution was the council's reaction to bloody clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops in which 56 Palestinians and 14 Israeli troops were killed after Israel opened a new entrance to a controversial archaeological tunnel near the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
The resolution did not specifically criticise Israel, but it implicitly called for the closing of the tunnel entrance and contained other elements to which Israel objected.

After referring in its preamble to the tunnel, the resolution called for the "immediate cessation and reversal of all acts" which aggravated the situation and had negative implications for the Middle East peace process.

Explaining her abstention, U.S. ambassador Madeleine Albright said the United States had been "working non-stop for the last 48 hours" to try to set up a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, and believed one was close.
"We want to make sure the people on the ground have every opportunity to come together," said Albright, whose country is the chief sponsor of the Middle East peace process.
"We think that is the most important part of what has to happen here, and therefore we believe that an abstention tonight was the appropriate action," she told reporters.

On Friday, Israel temporarily closed the underground passageway, intended as a window for tourists on centuries of history along the Western, or Wailing Wall, Judaism's holiest shrine. But Netanyahu said Saturday the tunnel "has been around for 2,000 years ... It will stay open."

During a day-long debate on Friday, the council heard a succession of speakers who criticised Israel's new right-wing government over the tunnel and accused it of dragging its feet on the peace process and of failing to implement agreements with the Palestinians by the previous Labour government.

On this, the council resolution called for the "immediate resumption of negotiations within the Middle East peace process on its agreed basis" and the "timely implementation of the agreements reached."
It also called for "the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be ensured."

Yitzhak Lior, a senior Israeli diplomat, said Israel "wishes to express its disappointment about this one-sided and unbalanced resolution, which did not even mention the Israeli casualties in the recent events..."

He said it did not advance the goals the Security Council was supposed to advance. While Israel had already said it was ready to renew negotiations with the Palestinians, "unfortunately this resolution will not be helpful."
He said the United States "did the utmost to balance the resolution. We appreciate it very much."

The Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. Observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, said: "We appreciate the fact that the Security Council was able to shoulder its responsibilities in this useful resolution. Now we hope that the Israeli government will understand the message and heed the requests contained in the resolution."
Expressing surprise at the U.S. abstention, he said: "We did work in good faith with all members of the council and we thought until the last minute we had in hand a unanimous resolution."
He said it was "time for the Israeli government to stop challenging the whole world and to try to integrate itself not only in the region but with the international system as well."

The resolution's preamble expressed deep concern about the "tragic events in Jerusalem and the areas of Nablus, Ramallah, Bethlehem and the Gaza Strip, which resulted in a high number of deaths and injuries among Palestinian civilians."
It also voiced concern about clashes between the Israeli army and Palestinian police and casualties on both sides.
